extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers, benchmark designers, and evaluators working on LLM story generation / creative-writing evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: A survey of quality dimensions, frameworks, and methodological lessons used to evaluate stories (especially in LLM/benchmark research). Summarizes common criteria, benchmark frameworks, and practical evaluation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuanced Characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of 14 core quality dimensions used across story-evaluation research; emphasizes depth and multi-faceted portrayal rather than flat or stereotyped characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotionally Engaging
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the story provokes authentic emotion in readers; often measured separately from overall engagement or empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling Plot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether plot events are organized and paced to sustain interest and story momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers global consistency of facts, timeline, and story logic; frequently operationalized in human annotations and automatic checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causally Sound
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires that story events have believable causal links (not merely superficially connected); often tested explicitly in some benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Intentionality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether characters' actions are motivated and interpretable as rational/intentional given their traits and the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic Conflict
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses presence and effectiveness of conflict or stakes that drive the narrative and character choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / Creativity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures novelty and inventiveness of plot, concept, or expression; appears across multiple frameworks including Torrance-derived dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks alignment to the given prompt or constraints (important in conditional generation evaluations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surface-level language quality (grammar, syntax, readability); often the easiest-to-measure dimension and included in many benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looks for twists or surprises that are both novel and well-supported by story context (i.e., 'earned' surprises).

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to emotionally engaging; focuses on whether readers can take the characters' perspectives and feel concern/compassion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures overall interest and the extent to which the story compels further reading; distinct from momentary emotional reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates thematic richness, layered characterization, and plot sophistication rather than simplistic or shallow narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTCW (Torrance-derived) Dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: 14 binary tests across 4 Torrance dimensions: Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, Elaboration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TTCW operationalizes creative-dimension testing as binary pass/fail checks mapped to Torrance creativity constructs; used for focused, discrete evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: HANNA 6-dim ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Human-Annotated NArratives benchmark with 6 rating dimensions: Relevance, Coherence, Empathy, Surprise, Engagement, Complexity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A human-annotated dataset used for multi-aspect rating; demonstrates grouping of common quality dimensions into a compact set for annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: EQ-Bench Longform Creative Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: multi-criteria human ratings of long-form creative writing with LLM-as-judge correlations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark for long-form stories using multiple human criteria; used to study how well LLM evaluators correlate with humans across aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: StoryER evaluation modes
rubrics_metrics.description: ranking, rating, and reasoning automatic evaluation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: StoryER provides multiple automatic evaluation paradigms (pairwise ranking, scalar rating, and rationale-based reasoning) to assess generated narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: OpenMEVA meta-evaluation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on evaluating evaluation methods themselves (meta-evaluation) to determine which metrics align with human judgments on open-ended text.

rubrics_metrics.name: UNION unreferenced metric approach
rubrics_metrics.description: unreferenced metric trained on synthetic negatives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A metric that does not rely on reference texts; it is trained to detect degraded/negative examples to assess quality without a ground-truth story.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAUVE distributional similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: measures distributional similarity between human and machine text
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statistical metric comparing generated text distribution to human text distribution; used to quantify overall generation 'human-likeness'.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-judge toolkits (GPTScore / G-Eval / G-Bench)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use large LMs to score or judge generated stories given explicit rubrics; shown to converge with humans when provided the same criterion definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SS-Bench (Social Stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: evaluation benchmark targeting social-story specific criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on social narrative aspects (e.g., social norms, interpersonal dynamics); illustrates domain-specific evaluation needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed rubrics improve reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed rubrics with criterion definitions improve evaluation reliability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological lesson: providing annotators (or LLM judges) with clear, fine-grained definitions reduces variance and increases agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-grained per-aspect evaluation over holistic ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Fine-grained per-aspect evaluation is preferable to a single overall rating
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically, aspect-level scores (e.g., coherence, characterization) produce more informative and reliable measurements than a single holistic quality score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation remains necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Human evaluation remains required for final judgments of quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite advances in automatic metrics and LLM-as-judge methods, humans are still needed for ultimate quality assessments, particularly for open-ended creative properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic metrics often misalign with humans
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic metrics often don't align with human judgment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A caution: distributional or reference-based metrics can diverge from human preferences on creativity, coherence, and other nuanced aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-as-judge alignment caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM-as-judge converges with human experts when given the same rubric
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LLM evaluators show strong correlation with experts only when provided explicit, detailed rubrics; without shared criteria, ratings diverge.

rubrics_metrics.name: No consensus on story evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no clear consensus on how to evaluate stories; even human experts using delimited criteria give divergent ratings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key finding motivating norm-discovery research: inherent subjectivity and disagreement remain major challenges for story-evaluation benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observed LLM strengths and weaknesses (empirical)
rubrics_metrics.description: GPT-4 outperforms GPT-3 on many human-eval comparisons but remains weak at sustained character intentionality, dramatic conflict, and long-context planning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical pattern: newer LLMs improve surface language alignment and situational handling, but deeper narrative skills (multi-turn planning, consistent motivations) need targeted evaluation and modeling.
